thread.title: what supplements should i take to fix my blood work?

parts.text: what supplements should i take to fix my blood work?

Looking at the plan, psyllium fibre is really the only formally recorded supplement, so I should stick to that rather than inventing recommendations for vitamin D or B12 that aren't backed by anything on file. I'll frame my answer around the one documented supplement while noting the key lab numbers—LDL at 131, ApoB at 99—that justify why fibre matters here, and ask what else they're currently taking before suggesting more.

Your fixable numbers are the lipids: LDL is 131 mg/dL (optimal is under 70), ApoB is 99 (optimal is under 80), and total cholesterol is 217. Fasting insulin of 5.7 is borderline, just above the optimal ceiling of 5. Vitamin D at 32.7 and B12 at 472 are inside the reference range and only slightly under optimal.

The only supplement in your plan is psyllium husk 10 g/day with about 70 g of oats [science], which should take LDL from 131 to roughly 110-118. The rest is food: protein and vegetables before the starch at each main meal [science]. If the repeat numbers still run high, ask your GP about atorvastatin 10-20 mg/day [opinion]. I have nothing on file that says vitamin D or B12 pills would fix your blood work.

Recheck the lipid panel, including ApoB, after 12 weeks. Tell me what supplements you already take, because that could change this.
